svg.title: An alternate key: a business value that addresses exactly one row
svg.desc: Top left, one Site row with its columns: the primary key cedar_siteid, a GUID that Dataverse assigns; the column cedar_sitecode with the value HV-LAB, which is the alternate key; the name and the account lookup. Top middle, the key definition: a name, cedar_sitecodekey; one to sixteen columns, here cedar_sitecode; allowed column types text, whole number, decimal, date and time, lookup and choice; at most 900 bytes in total; at most ten keys per table; a solution component. Top right, the index behind the key: a system job builds a unique index; the key status goes from Pending to In progress to Active, or to Failed when existing rows contain duplicates; only an Active key can address rows; after fixing the data, ReactivateEntityKey asks for the index again. Middle, four ways to name the same row: Web API by ID, Web API by key cedar_sites(cedar_sitecode='HV-LAB'), SDK new Entity("cedar_site", "cedar_sitecode", "HV-LAB") which fills KeyAttributes, and as a lookup value with odata.bind or an EntityReference built from the key. Bottom, what a key does not do: uniqueness is not enforced for rows whose key column is empty; the key covers inactive rows too; key columns cannot have column security, and virtual and elastic tables cannot have custom keys; values containing the characters slash, angle brackets, asterisk, percent, ampersand, colon, backslash, question mark, plus or hash cannot be addressed by key.
svg.text: An alternate key: a business value that addresses exactly one row
decimal, date and time, lookup, choice
Size: at most 900 bytes in total
with the table to Test and Prod
A system job builds a unique index.
Only an Active key addresses rows.
Four ways to name the same row
SDK: new EntityReference("cedar_site", "cedar_sitecode", "HV-LAB"). The GUID is stored.
What a key does not do
Empty values: uniqueness is not enforced for rows whose key column is empty.
Inactive rows count: the key covers every row of the table, not only the active ones.
No column security on key columns. No custom keys on virtual or elastic tables.
Values with / < > * % & : \ ? + # cannot be addressed by key: keep them out of key columns.
